signatureWindows.label: C-H absorption near 1.70 um
signatureWindows.meaning: Hydrocarbon-bearing materials can show absorption structure in this SWIR region. Broad multispectral bands are screening proxies only.

signatureWindows.label: C-H absorption near 2.30-2.35 um
signatureWindows.meaning: This is a stronger diagnostic SWIR window for petroleum/hydrocarbon signatures. Narrow hyperspectral bands are preferred.

sources.name: Sentinel-1 GRD SAR
sources.accessMethod: Open STAC search and open GRD assets; calibrated RTC processing may require a separate signed dataset
sources.hydrocarbonCapability: Surface roughness proxy, not chemical identification
sources.providerNote: Uses real Sentinel-1 STAC items and open band assets. SAR can flag dark slick candidates on water, but wind, look angle, biological slicks, rain cells, and ship wakes must be checked.
sources.notes: Oil on water can damp capillary waves and appear as a dark spot in VV/VH backscatter. This is the best free all-weather first screen for large water-surface slicks, but it cannot chemically identify hydrocarbon.

formulas.name: Adaptive VV Dark Spot
formulas.purpose: Candidate oil slick mask on open water

formulas.name: VV/VH Contrast
formulas.expression: VV_dB - VH_dB or VV / VH after calibration

workflow: Water slick: use VV/VH dark spots first, then compare to wind, ship lanes, and adjacent dates.
Long-term confirmation: compare multiple orbit passes before and after the suspected incident.
Hydrocarbon type: SAR cannot separate oil chemistry; it only sees surface roughness damping.
limitations: Low wind can create natural dark water that mimics oil.
Very small slicks below several pixels are not reliable at 10 m scale.

sources.name: Sentinel-2 MSI L2A
sources.spatialResolution: 10 m visible/NIR, 20 m SWIR, 60 m atmospheric
sources.accessMethod: Open STAC search and open COG tiles
sources.hydrocarbonCapability: Optical/SWIR proxy, not definitive chemical ID
sources.providerNote: Uses real Sentinel-2 L2A STAC items and Planetary Computer rendered band tiles. Cloud, sunglint, turbid water, wet soil, and shadows need manual review.
sources.notes: Sentinel-2 is useful for water masks, visible slick sheen context, SWIR moisture/oil stain contrast on coast and land, and repeat optical checks.

bands.name: Blue
bands.usage: True color, haze, shallow water context

bands.name: Green
bands.usage: Water mask and oil spill optical index

bands.name: SWIR 1
bands.usage: Oil stain, moisture, cloud shadow, and shoreline contrast

bands.name: SWIR 2
bands.usage: SWIR ratio proxy close to hydrocarbon absorption region

workflow: Water slick: mask water with NDWI, inspect visible bands and SWIR ratio, then cross-check with Sentinel-1.
Land/shore/apron stain: compare B11/B12 and NIR/SWIR against pre-event scenes.
Long archive: use repeated cloud-free scenes from 2015-present for persistence and cleanup monitoring.
limitations: 10-20 m pixels cannot reliably see narrow stains, small sheens, or thin linear leaks.
Hydrocarbon signature is only a proxy because MSI does not have narrow 2.30-2.35 um bands.

sources.name: Landsat 8/9 Collection 2 L2
sources.accessMethod: Open STAC search and open COG tiles
sources.hydrocarbonCapability: Long-term SWIR proxy and thermal context
sources.providerNote: Uses real Landsat Collection 2 Level-2 STAC items and Planetary Computer rendered band tiles. Best for larger features and long historical comparison.
sources.notes: Landsat is lower resolution than Sentinel-2 but has a strong long archive, SWIR bands, and thermal context for industrial/shoreline monitoring.

bands.name: Green
bands.usage: Water mask and visible oil index

bands.name: SWIR 2
bands.usage: SWIR ratio proxy close to hydrocarbon absorption region

bands.name: Thermal IR
bands.usage: Thermal context for large industrial surfaces

workflow: Long-term hindsight: build monthly/annual scene stacks from 2013-present.
Large land/coast stains: inspect SWIR1/SWIR2 before-after change against basemap context.
Water slick: use as supporting evidence when slick is broad enough for 30 m pixels.
limitations: 30 m pixels are usually too coarse for small apron stains or narrow shoreline contamination.
Cloud/shadow and wet ground can mimic oil in SWIR.

sources.name: EnMAP Hyperspectral
sources.accessMethod: EnMAP data portal / mission distribution; not wired to public tile rendering in this app
sources.hydrocarbonCapability: Direct narrow-band SWIR signature when an acquisition exists
sources.providerNote: This app lists real mission capability only. It does not synthesize EnMAP rasters or draw tiles without a live provider endpoint.
sources.notes: Hyperspectral SWIR is the right class of data for hydrocarbon signature work because it can sample narrow absorption features around 1.7 and 2.3 um.

formulas.name: Continuum-Removed Hydrocarbon Feature
formulas.purpose: Confirm absorption shape around C-H windows
requiredBands: SWIR narrow bands around 1.7 um or 2.3 um

workflow: Hydrocarbon signature: use continuum removal near 1.7 and 2.3 um on calibrated reflectance.
Use with Sentinel/Landsat: find candidate areas first, then validate with hyperspectral acquisition.
limitations: Coverage is not continuous everywhere and may require ordering or portal access.
30 m pixels still mix small stains with surrounding surface.

sources.name: PRISMA Hyperspectral
sources.accessMethod: ASI PRISMA portal / licensed distribution; not wired to public tile rendering in this app
sources.hydrocarbonCapability: Direct narrow-band SWIR signature when licensed imagery exists
sources.providerNote: This app lists real mission capability only. No PRISMA image is drawn unless a real provider endpoint is connected.
sources.notes: PRISMA is well suited to hydrocarbon spectral work when access and cloud-free coverage exist.

formulas.name: Hydrocarbon Absorption Depth
formulas.expression: continuum_removed_depth at 1.7 um and 2.3 um windows

workflow: Use Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2/Landsat to locate candidate stains.
Acquire cloud-free PRISMA scene and run spectral matching against field or library spectra.
limitations: Not an always-on global basemap source.
Licensing and access may limit operational use.

sources.name: WorldView-3 Visible/NIR/SWIR
sources.spatialResolution: About 0.3 m pan, 1.2 m VNIR, 3.7 m SWIR
sources.accessMethod: Maxar commercial order/API; not wired to public tile rendering in this app
sources.hydrocarbonCapability: High spatial detail with SWIR proxy bands
sources.providerNote: This app does not draw commercial imagery without a licensed provider endpoint. It records the real sensor option for apron/shoreline stains that are too small for free 10-30 m data.
sources.notes: WorldView-3 is the practical option when the target is an apron spill, tank-farm stain, narrow shoreline strip, or small land contamination patch.

bands.name: Panchromatic
bands.usage: Small stain shape and site context

bands.name: SWIR multispectral
bands.usage: Hydrocarbon and moisture proxy contrast at operational site scale

formulas.name: Before-After SWIR Change
formulas.expression: SWIR_current - SWIR_baseline, normalized by unchanged reference surfaces

workflow: Airport apron/industrial yard: use high-resolution pan/VNIR for shape and SWIR for material contrast.
Confirm with repeat tasked imagery and site photos or sampling.
Use free sensors first only for large context; they are usually too coarse for small spills.
limitations: SWIR is still multispectral, not full hyperspectral chemistry.
